name: High-Frequency Word Scanner
description: Scan the visible English text on a page, rank words by frequency, look up definitions from free English dictionaries, and export your selection as Markdown.

_comment_permissions.note: Documentation only. Keys that start with an underscore are ignored by Chrome; delete them if you prefer a bare manifest.
_comment_permissions.storage: Persists the scan payload, the saved selection, the settings, and the dictionary lookup cache locally. No sync, no remote storage.
_comment_permissions.host_permissions[0]: https://api.dictionaryapi.dev - primary dictionary provider (Free Dictionary API). Needed so the service worker can fetch without CORS restrictions.
_comment_permissions.host_permissions[1]: https://en.wiktionary.org - fallback dictionary provider (Wiktionary REST API).
_comment_permissions.host_permissions[2]: https://api.datamuse.com - optional gap filler for definitions and pronunciation hints.
_comment_permissions.content_scripts.matches: Declares the injection target, which is also the only broad host access this extension asks for. It is what places the floating scan button on a page. Without it the button could only appear after a manual click on the toolbar icon.
not_requested: tabs - not needed. The source URL and title come from the content script, and chrome.tabs.create / chrome.tabs.sendMessage work without it.
downloads - not needed. The Markdown file is produced with a Blob plus an anchor element on the results page.
scripting - not needed. The content script is declared declaratively and the results page messages the tab that already runs it.
webRequest - not needed. All dictionary traffic goes through the service worker with host_permissions, so there is nothing to rewrite.
unlimitedStorage - not needed. The scan payload is roughly 0.5 MB, and the optional WordNet subset lives in IndexedDB, not in chrome.storage.local.

_comment_privacy.page_content: Never uploaded. Text is tokenized in the tab and the token list is written to chrome.storage.local on this device.
_comment_privacy.network: The only outbound requests are dictionary lookups issued from the service worker for words the user opened or exported.
